corrections.correction: raw_orders amounts (subtotal, tax_paid, order_total) are stored in CENTS. Use stg_orders which converts to dollars, or divide raw values by 100. stg_orders also keeps _cents columns (subtotal_cents, tax_paid_cents, order_total_cents) if you need both.
raw_orders uses 'customer' (not customer_id), 'id' (not order_id), and 'store_id' (not location_id). Downstream models rename these: customer→customer_id, id→order_id, store_id→location_id.

orders has multiple amount columns: order_total (includes tax), subtotal (pre-tax), order_items_subtotal (sum of product prices), order_cost (sum of supply costs). Choose carefully based on what you need. order_total = subtotal + tax_paid.

customers.customer_type is either 'new' (first order only) or 'returning' (more than one order). Use exact strings. is_repeat_buyer is a boolean in the intermediate calculation but customer_type is the final column.

Food/drink classification comes from products (is_food_item, is_drink_item). order_items inherits these. orders has is_food_order and is_drink_order booleans plus count_food_items/count_drink_items. A single order can be both food AND drink.

customers table has pre-computed lifetime metrics: lifetime_spend (with tax), lifetime_spend_pretax, lifetime_tax_paid, count_lifetime_orders. No need to re-aggregate from orders. lifetime_spend = lifetime_spend_pretax + lifetime_tax_paid.
product_price is what the customer pays per item. supply_cost is what it costs to produce. Margin = product_price - supply_cost. These are on order_items (mart), not on raw_items.
customers table has pre-computed first_ordered_at and last_ordered_at TIMESTAMP columns. No need to join to orders for these.
raw_items uses 'sku' for product and 'id' for item PK. stg_order_items renames: id→order_item_id, sku→product_id. Always use staging/mart column names unless querying raw directly.
orders.customer_order_number is a row_number() per customer ordered by date. customer_order_number=1 means first order. Use this to identify first-time vs repeat purchases at the order level.
